segments.source: Fast Forward is a recurring blend built around seasonal organic coffee, not a single-origin lot. Counter Culture says it chooses similar coffees from different harvest periods to keep a nutty, sweet and creamy brief. The current product record names washed processing and a broad Latin America and Africa sourcing scope. Its roast-date selector is the place to identify the specific bag; the accessible text lists several historical component pairs without a reliable one-to-one binding to every selector choice, so we do not assign percentages to a future bag.

segments.source: “Nutty,” “sweet” and “creamy” are Counter Culture’s sensory words. They are a selection brief, not flavors Coffeedant found in a tasting. The Guardian’s August 2026 multi-coffee comparison provides an independent sample perspective on Counter Culture’s range, but a single published cup cannot stabilize a rotating blend. A self-selected owner described Fast Forward as a reliable grocery-store choice; another liked its balanced sweet acidity. Neither experience predicts this bag or establishes a satisfaction rate.

segments.source: The useful judgment is about risk: this profile is less of a fruit gamble than Hologram or Apollo, while the medium roast leaves more room for a lighter finish than a dark blend. If your idea of a breakfast coffee is smoky or very bitter, the stated brief points elsewhere. If you want the highest possible origin specificity, choose a dated single-origin instead of using Fast Forward’s name as a guarantee.

segments.source: Counter Culture explicitly names both auto-drip and espresso. It suggests 1 g coffee to 17 g water for most brewing devices. For filter coffee, 20 g coffee with about 340 g water is a transparent starting calculation. It is not an espresso recipe: a portafilter needs a much shorter beverage ratio and a grind adjusted to the actual basket and bag. Do not take a filter ratio into an espresso machine.

The page describes direct relationships and a washed-process harvest summary, plus a roast-date selector with multiple periods.
